title: Windows Management Instrumentation and CIM
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Windows Management Instrumentation and CIM and define its core vocabulary.
Apply windows management instrumentation and cim in a small PowerShell example and predict its result.
Identify one relevant edge case, version constraint, or troubleshooting step.

content.intro: This lesson covers Windows Management Instrumentation and CIM in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Windows administration commands can alter important machine state. Start with read-only inventory, constrain targets, verify permissions, and check the result after any approved change. The Windows Registry, Active Directory, services and event logs are Windows-specific capabilities.

content_blocks.troubleshooting: Check command availability with Get-Command, inspect values with Get-Member, consult Get-Help -Full, and verify PowerShell version/platform before assuming identical output. Do not run examples that change system state without adapting and reviewing them.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.
